proposed_from.topic: Blind replicated continuous-treatment ADRF over a fixed quantitative class. Observe finite-stratum X, bounded Y, and S_r=A+U_r; the centered independent nonidentical asymmetric errors have a uniform q>=8 moment radius and fixed near-origin characteristic-function lower modulus but may have open spectral zeros. Compact A support supplies the analytic source radius; latent densities f_x and outcome-weighted measures q_x have fixed H^beta radii with beta>3/2 and f_x is bounded below near the target interval. Prove analytic-cocycle identification of f_x, q_x, and mu(a)=sum_x P(X=x)q_x(a)/f_x(a), then construct a uniformly honest simultaneous band with width r_n=(log log n/log n)^(beta-1/2) and prove a matching all-honest-band expected-width converse. Use empirical-CF confidence-set inversion and constrained analytic sieves. Consumer: Melaku-Shi 2026 NHANES two-recall diet-mortality mvGPS. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact identities give F_x(s,t)=fhat_x(s+t)phi_1(s)phi_2(t) and G_x(s,t)=qhat_x(s+t)phi_1(s)phi_2(t); their ratios and cocycle recover the centered latent and outcome-weighted transforms near zero, with analyticity extending globally. At the EJS cutoff T_n of order log n/log log n, Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz yields the candidate sup-norm scale T_n^(1/2-beta), transferred through f_x>=kappa. The sinc^12 asymmetric witness, denominator, contamination, signed-measure, and prior-art checks all survived independently. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Establish the matching outcome-channel modulus by constructing contiguous Bernoulli-outcome alternatives with fixed positive f and compact-spectrum errors whose dose-response curves differ by cT_n^(1/2-beta), and match it with a uniformly honest band of width CT_n^(1/2-beta). EARLY KILL TEST: In one X cell with known smooth positive f, fixed sinc^12 errors, and Bernoulli mean 1/2+g(a), compute the singular-value modulus over an H^beta ball at degree log n/log log n; pivot if the H^beta-to-L-infinity separation differs from m^(1/2-beta) or outcomes permit a faster honest-band rate.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The foundational unknown-error repeated-measurement lineage is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. LiVuong1998, Assumptions A1--A3, Lemma 2.1, and equations (1)--(8) on pp. 140--143, already identifies and estimates latent and error densities from repeated indicators under global nonvanishing; Theorems 3.1--3.4 on pp. 147--151 already give uniform rates. Schennach2004, equations (7)--(8), Assumptions 1--4, and Theorem 1 with equations (11)--(16) on pp. 1049--1051, already identifies the smoothed regression numerator and denominator from repeated measurements under global nonvanishing, while Assumption 8 and Theorems 2--3 on pp. 1056--1063 give pointwise rates and asymptotic normality. DelaigleHallMeister2008, equations (2.1)--(2.6), condition (2.2), and Theorems 3.1 and 3.5 on pp. 668--676, already recovers density and regression point estimators from a common replicate-error law and proves first-order equivalence to known-error procedures under its real-valued nowhere-zero ordinary- or supersmooth operator conditions. Thus unknown-error repeated-measurement regression, replicate-based error-law recovery, regression numerator--denominator deconvolution, and nonvanishing ordinary- or supersmooth regression estimation are not contributions of this project. The first novelty claim is joint analytic identification of the compact-support latent density and shared signed outcome-weighted channel under blind nonidentical asymmetric errors whose characteristic functions may have open zero sets, with recovery of their continuous Sobolev representatives and pointwise causal ADRF recovery through the declared continuity bridge. CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025, Theorem 1 on pp. 4141--4173, recovers a latent probability law and error laws over a broader H2 exponential-moment/tail class; the present local \(G_x/F_x\) transfer, signed-measure continuation, and stable division add the shared outcome channel only on its compact-support submodel and do not extend its latent-law class. The fixed common local-modulus constants are a maintained quantitative class restriction: continuity and \(\phi_r(0)=1\) provide only distribution-specific constants, and CapitaoMiniconiGassiatLehericy2025 is not invoked as support for uniform \(\nu\) and \(c_{\phi}\). This restriction is not counted as a novelty claim. Consistency and weak unconfoundedness first identify \(m_x^{\mathrm{pot}}=q_x/f_x\) almost everywhere, and positivity plus separately maintained continuity promote equality pointwise; potential-mean continuity neither aids analytic recovery nor determines the rate. The second novelty claim is a uniformly honest simultaneous causal ADRF band from coupled inversion of stratum masses, latent densities, signed outcome channels, and both blind error laws in the open-zero regime, with expected supremum width \(r_n\). LiVuong1998, Schennach2004, DelaigleHallMeister2008, KatoSasakiUra2021, and KatoSasaki2019 provide density estimation, pointwise regression inference, or conventional-operator bands but not this open-zero coupled causal band. The third novelty claim is the matching all-honest expected-width converse on the fixed noisy-treatment marginal. Its admissible uniform vector \(p_x^{\star}=|\mathcal X_0|^{-1}\), common \(f_0\), fixed nonidentical asymmetric compact-spectrum errors, and identical smooth Bernoulli perturbation in every stratum keep the full law of \((X,S_1,S_2)\) fixed, avoid stratum attenuation, and leave product-experiment total variation unchanged. Strict positivity and Sobolev-radius margins make this hard subclass nonempty. Published latent-density lower bounds and generic confidence-length inequalities do not supply that outcome-channel construction. HuangZhang2023, Sections 2--3 on pp. 474--496, is the already-known known-error ADRF result; the dependent benchmark proposition is non-root, excluded from the research theorem count, and carries no novelty claim.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and its analytic-cocycle proof, Theorems 2 and 4, the Legendre lower-bound construction, and the Discussion were read from the arXiv source. The proof first cancels the two noise factors locally, derives a multiplicative cocycle for the signal transform, fixes the translation, and extends equality by analyticity. Its lower bound perturbs the latent density and controls observed total variation through compact-spectrum noise.
seed_details.opportunity: Jointly identify the latent density and outcome-weighted subdensity, then characterize the minimax expected width of every honest ADRF band over one fixed quantitative class.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The positive-density perturbation in the published lower bound is replaced by a mean-zero perturbation of the Bernoulli outcome channel while the latent density and both error laws stay fixed; the observed divergence is therefore controlled through the weighted transform rather than the noisy-treatment marginal.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for blind repeated-measurement regression bands, ADRF bands with unknown error laws, and outcome-weighted analytic deconvolution found no paper combining open spectral zeros, simultaneous causal regression inference, and an all-honest-band converse.
adjacent_threads: KatoSasaki2019 for simultaneous EIV regression bands
HuangZhang2023 for the causal ADRF functional
LouniciNickl2011 and Low1997 for sup-norm separation and expected-width conversion
seed_details.deep_novelty_check: The adjacent papers settle, separately, robust density coverage, ordinary-smooth regression coverage, known-error causal estimation, and known-operator minimax risk. None keeps the treatment marginal and blind operator fixed while deriving both an ADRF upper band and an all-honest expected-width lower bound.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehericy because their minimax density theorem already gives the logarithmic rate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their alternatives change the noisy-treatment marginal and their loss is latent-density \(L^2\); the proposed fixed-marginal Bernoulli alternatives, signed outcome channel, ADRF ratio, simultaneous coverage, and expected-width conclusion are absent.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names the analytic continuation modulus and the outcome-channel hard family, is uniform over a quantitative class, and includes both a construction and a converse.
seed_details.burned_reason: Angle 0 exhausted nine revisions and the operator-directed final repair still returned an assumption-attribution flag.

seed_details.anchor_read: The same source receipt was used, with special attention to Theorem 1 and the local phase-additivity argument in its proof.
seed_details.opportunity: Prove injectivity of the shared-error map simultaneously for a probability density and a bounded signed outcome-weighted measure, followed by causal division on the positive-density interval.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After the latent phase is fixed, positivity and unit mass no longer normalize the outcome channel; uniqueness instead comes from the observable ratio \(G_x/F_x\) on a neighborhood of zero and analytic continuation of a compactly supported signed measure.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact pair signed outcome-weighted measure plus blind replicate cocycle returned density-identification papers and known-error regression papers, but no joint injectivity theorem.
adjacent_threads: EvdokimovWhite2012 for Kotlarski identification at zeros
HuangZhang2023 for the outcome-weighted causal target
seed_details.deep_novelty_check: Evdokimov and White do not cover the finite-moment open-zero regime, Kato, Sasaki, and Ura do not introduce a weighted channel, and Huang and Zhang take the error transform as known. No closer injectivity theorem subsumes the signed-channel claim.
seed_details.red_team: The weighted channel is just the density theorem with \(Y\) attached.
seed_details.rebuttal: A signed subprobability is not normalized as a latent law, and its uniqueness must be proved through cross-channel compatibility before division; nevertheless this seed alone is narrower than the chosen matched inference kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: It is not bare identification because it specifies the new signed-channel uniqueness step, but it lacks an inference rung when isolated.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorem 1 on linear complex moments, Theorems 2 through 4 on size, approximation, and power, their proofs, and the Conclusion were read from the arXiv source. The construction discretizes complex moments, adds sieve-bias slack, calibrates a self-normalized maximum by multiplier bootstrap, and projects an Anderson--Rubin confidence set.
seed_details.opportunity: Invert coupled unweighted and outcome-weighted empirical characteristic-function restrictions over compact-support analytic sieves and obtain a rate-explicit ADRF band.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The scalar density moment system becomes a coupled feasible set for \(f_x\), \(q_x\), and two nonidentical error laws, and its projected diameter must be bounded after the nonlinear map \(q_x/f_x\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for empirical-characteristic-function inversion of a regression numerator and denominator at open spectral zeros found no rate-explicit simultaneous band.
adjacent_threads: KatoSasaki2019 for multiplier EIV regression bands
seed_details.deep_novelty_check: The available methods do not compose automatically because direct Fourier division is undefined at open zero intervals and qualitative confidence-set consistency does not bound the nonlinear projected diameter. The exact coupled inversion remains unoccupied.
seed_details.red_team: Kato, Sasaki, and Ura already construct a robust confidence band without completeness.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their band covers a latent density and establishes size and consistency without a sharp shrinking rate; it neither treats a weighted outcome channel nor propagates a joint feasible set through an ADRF ratio.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The rate and projected feasible-set diameter are named focal objects, so this is not a bare inference add-on.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorem 1, Theorems 3 through 5, the Meyer-wavelet packing proof of the lower bound, and the confidence-band discussion were read from the arXiv source. The proof calibrates sup-norm separation by a half-derivative localization gain and bounds Kullback--Leibler divergence after convolution.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct fixed-treatment-marginal, fixed-error Bernoulli alternatives that force every uniformly honest ADRF band to have width \(m_n^{1/2-\beta}\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The known convolution operator and translated wavelet packing are replaced by a compact-spectrum two-replicate operator and high-degree Legendre outcome perturbations whose low-frequency transform is superexponentially small.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for honest-band expected-width lower bounds in blind nonparametric EIV regression found minimax estimation lower bounds and known-operator bands, but no fixed-marginal outcome-channel modulus.
adjacent_threads: KatoSasakiUra2021 for the absence of a sharp unrestricted Kotlarski rate
seed_details.deep_novelty_check: The latent-density and known-operator lower bounds both change an observed treatment distribution. The proposed experiment fixes it, so no inspected lower bound subsumes the Bernoulli outcome-channel modulus.
seed_details.red_team: The lower bound follows mechanically from the known-error sup-norm deconvolution packing.
seed_details.rebuttal: Known-error packings perturb a density under an invertible nonvanishing operator; here the hard family must preserve the entire noisy-treatment law and satisfy Bernoulli probability constraints while exploiting a noninvertible compact-spectrum channel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The witness is a sequence inside a fixed nondegenerate subclass, not a single hand-tuned law.

seed_details.anchor_read: The adaptive-estimation theorem and the Discussion on selecting the local radius to exploit ordinary-smooth noise were read in addition to the main source receipt.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct one honest ADRF band over the open-zero class that attains each nested spectral subclass's own minimax width when the error transforms happen to be nonvanishing and ordinary smooth.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Goldenshluger--Lepski selection of a point estimator must be replaced by selection among confidence sets using empirical lower envelopes for the error-transform modulus while preserving coverage over the union.
seed_details.destination_search: Adaptive deconvolution bands exist for known operators, while Low-type results obstruct unrestricted smoothness adaptation; no result was found for adaptation to blind spectral strength with fixed Sobolev smoothness.
adjacent_threads: LouniciNickl2011 for adaptation under known operator classes
KatoSasaki2019 for data-driven regularization under ordinary-smooth errors
seed_details.deep_novelty_check: No source settles adaptation across unknown blind operator-strength subclasses. Because the needed separation frontier is unresolved, the candidate is retained only as an open-ended question and not as a promised theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Uniform honesty over the broad class makes faster adaptation impossible by Low's theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Low rules out unrestricted adaptation across smoothness classes, not necessarily adaptation across separated operator-strength subclasses; the separation condition and exact frontier remain open and are retained only as an open-ended question.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not asserted as a theorem; it has a concrete empirical spectral-envelope handle and explicitly exposes the adaptation obstruction.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Gaussian-approximation and multiplier-band theorems, their proof architecture, the supersmooth limitation, and the Conclusion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.opportunity: Obtain a simultaneous band and matched rate for the marginal causal response \(\mu'(a)\) under blind open-zero replicates.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The analytic continuation bound must be differentiated before Sobolev embedding, changing the deterministic tail from \(m^{1/2-\beta}\) to \(m^{3/2-\beta}\) and requiring \(\beta>5/2\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for derivative ADRF inference with treatment measurement error found pointwise curve inference but no open-zero derivative band.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine derivative-loss corollary of the level-band proof.
seed_details.rebuttal: Differentiated continuation changes the admissible smoothness and hard modulus, but the consumer gain does not compensate for its narrower scope.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The changed modulus is named, but the direction is too close to the primary proof once that proof exists.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, ADRF identification formula, ordinary- and supersmooth asymptotic theorems, simulation conclusion, and NHANES application were read from the arXiv source. The paper identifies an ADRF through weighted conditional expectations and performs known-error Fourier deconvolution with pointwise inference.
seed_details.opportunity: Replace \(Y\) by \(1\{Y\le y\}\) and identify and band the full distributional dose-response surface jointly over dose and outcome threshold.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The single weighted transform becomes a two-index empirical process, and the continuation diameter must be controlled uniformly in a bounded-variation threshold index as well as dose.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for distributional dose-response bands with replicated treatment error found conditional-distribution EIV extensions but no blind open-zero causal surface.
seed_details.red_team: Thresholding the outcome makes the result an immediate vector-index extension.
seed_details.rebuttal: The additional threshold process is not algebraically difficult, and without a new two-dimensional modulus the advance would be mostly technical; the seed is therefore dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The cynical objection holds at the current level of evidence.

seed_details.anchor_read: The same Huang--Zhang source receipt was combined with the Kato--Sasaki--Ura complex-moment construction; the paper's pointwise linear expansion was checked against the proposed blind nuisance.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive an observed-data Neyman-orthogonal score for a smoothed ADRF with high-dimensional covariates and an unknown blind replicate operator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The nuisance tangent for the unknown pair of error laws must be projected through the coupled analytic moment restrictions before the usual continuous-treatment score can be orthogonalized.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found corrected scores under known Gaussian error and recent proximal dose-response bands, but no orthogonal score for a blind nonparametric replicate operator with spectral zeros.
seed_details.red_team: This merely combines a continuous-treatment doubly robust score with Kotlarski inversion.
seed_details.rebuttal: The operator nuisance changes the tangent space and may preclude a regular influence function; because no candidate score or pathwise-differentiability result survived the first check, this angle is not yet well posed.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is dropped rather than presented as a bare high-dimensional extension.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Discussion's extension from two to \(p\) measurements and the corresponding blockwise contrast were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize whether a growing number of replicates changes the logarithmic ADRF-band rate or only its constant.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The two-factor cocycle would be replaced by a \(p\)-factor contrast and the information radius recalculated under a measurement-budget constraint.
seed_details.destination_search: Repeated-measurement deconvolution papers already treat multiple replicates, and no evidence indicated a new rate when the number of replicates is fixed.
seed_details.red_team: The fixed-\(p\) extension is already noted by Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehericy and follows by pairing coordinates.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for fixed \(p\); a growing-\(p\) budget frontier would require a different sampling design not present in the topic.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped as a routine replication-count extension.
